mechanismOfAction:
How LIGNOCAD 2% GEL Works

LIGNOCAD 2% GEL is a local anaesthetic agent. It reduces pain sensation and causes numbness in body parts by blocking the flow of certain ions (sodium ions) through the nerves that cause pain sensation. As a result, it limits the transfer of pain signals from the peripheral part of the body (i.e., the face, hands, legs, abdomen, pelvis, genitals, or where the medicine has been applied) to the brain, which ultimately leads to loss of sensation.
usageDetails:
How to use LIGNOCAD 2% GEL

LIGNOCAD 2% GEL should be used under proper medical supervision. It is administered by the physician in the region where anesthesia is required. However, it can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor.

Take a small quantity of LIGNOCAD 2% GEL and apply it to the required areas. Avoid contact with LIGNOCAD 2% GEL with your eyes.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight, health condition, and sites where numbness is required in the body.

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before using LIGNOCAD 2% GEL, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines, such as:

Mexiletine, amiodarone (used to manage an uneven heartbeat)
Cimetidine (a medicine used to manage stomach ulcers)
Beta-blockers such as atenolol, propranolol, and bisoprolol (used to manage high blood pressure)
Nitrates (such as nitric oxide and nitroglycerin) are used to improve blood flow
Other local anaesthetic agents (such as bupivacaine, proparacaine, ropivacaine, mepivacaine, prilocaine, procaine, and tetracaine)
Antibiotics (used to manage bacterial infections) such as PABA, nitrofurantoin, dapsone, and sulfasalazine
Anticancer medicines (used to manage cancer) such as cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, hydroxyurea, flutamide, and rasburicase
Antimalarial agents (used to manage malarial infection) Ex. chloroquine, primaquine, and quinine
Anti-epileptic agents (used to manage fits) Ex. phenytoin, sodium valproate, phenobarbital
Metoclopramide (a medicine used to manage nausea and vomiting)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else has applied excessive LIGNOCAD 2% GEL, wipe off the excess with a paper towel or tissue paper. If your child or anyone else accidentally swallowed LIGNOCAD 2% GEL, contact your doctor immediately or visit a nearby hospital immediately, as it may lead to a severe decrease in low blood pressure.

name: Critifol 1% Infusion 50ml
introduction:
Introduction About CRITIFOL 1% INFUSION

CRITIFOL 1% INFUSION contains Propofol which belongs to the group of medicines called General Anaesthetic agents. It is used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness in patients so that surgical procedures can be performed. Unconsciousness caused by propofol is completely reversed once the effect of the medicine wears off. It can also be used to induce sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

CRITIFOL 1% INFUSION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anesthesiologist into the vein (intravenously). It is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 1 month or older). It is mostly used in combination with other local anaesthetics to achieve faster results.

Before receiving CRITIFOL 1% INFUSION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have fits, high blood cholesterol levels or dehydration as a precaution.

CRITIFOL 1% INFUSION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Breastfeeding should be stopped for 24 hours or until the effect of the medicine completely wears off, as this medicine may pass to the nursing infant through the breast milk.

The most common side effects of receiving CRITIFOL 1% INFUSION are pain, swelling and redness at the site of injection, low blood pressure, slow heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, headache and flushing. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

name: LOX VISCOUS 2% Oral Solution 100ml
introduction:
Introduction About LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION contains Lignocaine which belongs to the group of medicines called Local Anaesthetics. It is used to cause numbness in the oral cavity. It provides pain relief and reduces discomfort in the oral cavity when the mucosal membranes of the mouth or the throat have been inflamed, irritated, or infected.

It also anesthetizes the oral cavity, respiratory tract, and digestive tract prior to the insertion of catheters or certain instruments used during diagnostic procedures (such as bronchoscopy or esophagoscopy). It also helps in managing gag reflux (vomiting sensation) that occurs during dental procedures (such as X-rays of the oral cavity or dental impressions).

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION may also help in reducing pain and discomfort that is associated with problems of the upper gastrointestinal tract, such as esophagitis (inflammation of the food pipe).

Following the administration of LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION, avoid oral foods or chewing gums for at least 60 minutes or until sensation comes back in your mouth. This is because you may experience trouble swallowing or accidentally bite your tongue or cheek muscles during this period. Do not drink water or other fluids after applying LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION, as it may reduce its anaesthetic effects.

Before using LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION, inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney, or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have a severe injury or bleeding in the mouth, throat, or epilepsy before using LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION.

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION should be used in pregnant or breastfeeding women only if it is considered necessary by the physician. The most common side effects of using LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION are irritation or itching at the site of application, which is usually mild and disappears once the anaesthetic effect begins. However, consult your doctor if it bothers you.

Relieve pain, discomfort, irritation, and inflammation of the mouth, throat (pharynx), or esophagus
Prevent gag reflux (vomiting sensation) during dental procedures

mechanismOfAction:
How LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION Works

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION is a local anaesthetic agent. It reduces pain sensation and causes numbness in body parts by blocking the flow of certain ions (sodium ions) through the nerves that cause pain sensation. As a result, it limits the transfer of pain signals from the peripheral part of the body (i.e., the face, hands, legs, abdomen, pelvis, or where the medicine has been applied) to the brain, which ultimately leads to loss of sensation.
usageDetails:
How to use LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION should be used under proper medical supervision. It is usually administered by the physician after proper dilutions. However, it may also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor.

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION is for oral topical use only where patients may be advised to swish or gargle the medicine within the mouth followed by spitting out. However, your doctor may also ask you to swallow the medicine if numbness of the throat or respiratory/digestive tract is involved.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose, duration of therapy, or frequency of administration for you depending upon your age, body weight, health condition, and sites where numbness is required in the body.

warnings.details: LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION should be used in pregnant women only if it is considered necessary by the physician. Therefore, inform your doctor before using LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION if you are pregnant or think you may be pregnant.

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION should be used for breastfeeding women only if it is considered necessary by the physician. Therefore, inform your doctor before using LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION if you are breastfeeding.
LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION does not affect your ability to drive or operate any heavy tools or machines when used at prescribed doses.
LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Therefore, inform your doctor before using it.
LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION should be used with caution in patients with liver problems. Therefore, inform your doctor before using it.
Inform your doctor before using LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION if you are allergic to lignocaine.

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION should be used with caution in patients with heart diseases (such as abnormal or slow heartbeat, heart block, cardiac arrest, etc.). Therefore, inform your doctor before using it.

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION can be used in children and adolescents (aged between 3-18 years). It should be used in children aged below 3 years only if prescribed by the physician. Your doctor will prescribe a suitable dose for your child based on their age, body weight, health condition, and capacity for spitting and swallowing. It is generally not used to soothe teething pain in infants. However, consult your doctor for advice.

LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION should be used with caution with elderly patients. Your doctor will prescribe the appropriate dose for you based on your age, body weight, and sites where numbness is required in the body.

Others

Before using LOX VISCOUS 2% ORAL SOLUTION, inform your physician if you:

Have a severe injury or bleeding in the mouth or throat
Have epilepsy (fits)
Have severe shock (sudden loss of blood flow in the body)
Have an acute illness or infection (sepsis)
Have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (a genetic disorder that affects red blood cells).
Have methemoglobinemia (build up toxic proteins in the blood)
Have porphyria (an inherited blood disorder)

introduction:
Introduction About LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION contains Lignocaine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Local anaesthetic agents. It is used to cause numbness (loss of sensation) of body parts in the regions where it has been administered (local anesthesia). It is generally used prior to spinal anesthesia or before surgical procedures to cause a temporary loss of sensation. It also helps to control the heartbeat in patients with arrythmia (an irregular heartbeat).

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION will be given to you only by a trained anaesthesiologist around the areas (such as hands, legs, abdomen, pelvis, and spine) locally where loss of sensation (numbness) is required.

Before receiving LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION, inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney, or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any breathing disorders, blood problems, epilepsy, glaucoma, stroke, dehydration, low blood potassium levels, or muscle weakness.

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION should be used in pregnant or breastfeeding women only if considered necessary by the physician. The most common side effects of receiving LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION are nausea, slow heart rate, dizziness, lower back pain, difficulty walking, and an inability to control urine or bowel movements. Inform your doctor if any of these side effects worsen.
uses: Causes numbness of body parts when used prior to spinal anesthesia or surgical procedures
To manage arrythmia (an irregular heartbeat)
usesDetails:
Uses Of LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION
Causes numbness of body parts when used prior to spinal anesthesia or surgical procedures
To manage arrythmia (an irregular heartbeat)
mechanismOfAction:
How LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION Works

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION is an anaesthetic agent. It reduces pain sensation and causes numbness in body parts by blocking the flow of certain ions (sodium ions) through the nerves that cause pain sensation. As a result, it limits the transfer of pain signals from the peripheral parts of the body (i.e., the face, hands, legs, abdomen, and pelvis) to the brain, which leads to a loss of sensation. It also normalizes heart rate by blocking the generation of abnormal electrical signals in the heart.
usageDetails:
How to use LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anaesthesiologist. Your doctor or anaesthesiologist will decide the correct dose and site of administration for you depending upon your age, body weight, health condition, and the type of nerve block that is required to provide anesthesia or pain relief.

It can be administered locally to the region where loss of sensation (numbness) is required or can be administered in a vein, around the spinal cord, or a nerve to cause numbness during surgeries (caesarean section or other major surgeries) to stop pain sensation.

warnings.details: LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION should be used in pregnant women only if it is considered necessary by the physician. Therefore, inform your doctor if you are pregnant or think you may be pregnant before receiving LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION.

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION should be used for breastfeeding women only if it is considered necessary by the physician. Therefore, inform your doctor before receiving LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION if you are breastfeeding.

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION may make you feel dizzy or drowsy for some time after administration. Therefore, do not drive or operate any heavy tools or machines if your abilities are affected by LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION.
Avoid the consumption of alcohol before receiving LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION.
LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION should be used with caution in patients with liver problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
Inform your doctor before receiving LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION if you are allergic to lignocaine or to any other local anaesthetics (such as bupivacaine).
LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION should be used with caution in patients with breathing disorders (such as asthma or COPD). Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with heart diseases (such as heart block, an abnormal heartbeat, or a very slow heartbeat). It should be used with caution in patients with other heart disorders. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION should be used in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) only if it is considered necessary by the physician. It is not recommended for use in neonates aged less than 1 month. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before administration.
LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION should be used with caution with elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before receiving it.

Others

LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION is not recommended for use if you:

Have low blood volume
Have porphyria (an inherited blood disorder)

Before receiving LIGNOCAINE(CADILA) INJECTION, inform your physician if you:

Are feeling sick or tired for no reason
Have epilepsy (fits)
Have glaucoma
Have low potassium levels in the blood, causing muscle cramps and constipation
Recently had vomiting, diarrhea, or excessive blood loss
Are not drinking enough amount of water
Have too much acidity in the blood
Have any skin infection (with pus) in and around the areas where the medicine is planned to be administered
Have problems thinking or reasoning
Have myasthenia gravis (severe muscle weakness or tenderness)
Have stroke
Have an imbalance in the constituents of the blood
Have a blood disorder

introduction:
Introduction About PROPOVAN 1% INJECTION

PROPOVAN 1% INJECTION contains Propofol which belongs to the group of medicines called General Anaesthetic agents. It is used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness in patients so that surgical procedures can be performed. Unconsciousness caused by propofol is completely reversed once the effect of the medicine wears off. It can also be used to induce sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

PROPOVAN 1% INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anesthesiologist into the vein (intravenously). It is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 1 month or older). It is mostly used in combination with other local anaesthetics to achieve faster results.

Before receiving PROPOVAN 1% INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have fits, high blood cholesterol levels or dehydration as a precaution.

PROPOVAN 1% INJECTION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Breastfeeding should be stopped for 24 hours or until the effect of the medicine completely wears off, as this medicine may pass to the nursing infant through the breast milk.

The most common side effects of receiving PROPOVAN 1% INJECTION are pain, swelling and redness at the site of injection, low blood pressure, slow heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, headache and flushing. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

introduction:
Introduction About ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION

ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION contains Isoflurane which belongs to a group of medicines known as General Anaesthetics. ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is used for induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia during surgeries.

General Anaesthesia can be defined as a state of controlled unconsciousness. There is temporary reduction in activity of central nervous system in brain which in result causes complete loss of sensation in body and loss of consciousness, which is required during surgery.

ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is not recommended for use in patients with or family history of rapid rise in body temperature during anaesthesia (a condition known as malignant hyperthermia). ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in patients having liver, heart, kidney or lung problems, increased intracranial pressure, myasthenia gravis (muscle weakness) or diabetes.

ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless it is clearly necessary. ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it is not known whether it passes through the breast milk. ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in children so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in elderly patients aged above 65 years. The most common side effects of using ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION are agitation, breath holding, chills or shivering, cough, change in mental abilities, spasm of vocal cords, nausea and vomiting. Consult your physician in case any of the symptoms worsen.

Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before administration of ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Medicines used for management of high blood pressure and heart diseases (Ex. labetalol, acebutolol, atenolol, nifedipine, verapamil, amlodipine)
Opioids such as codeine, fentanyl, tramadol (used for management of severe pain)
Zolpidem, zopiclone (medicines used for management of insomnia)
Epinephrine, isoprenaline, ephedrine, norepinephrine (medicines for management of hypersensitivity, heart diseases, respiratory problems, etc.)
Amphetamine, dextroamphetamine (medicines used for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder)
Ephedrine (used for decongestion)
Isoniazid (used for management of tuberculosis)
Phenelzine, selegiline, isocarboxazid, St. John’s Wort (medicines used for management of depression)
Succinylcholine, atracurium, pancuronium, rocuronium, vecuronium (muscle relaxants used in anaesthesia)
Inhalational anaesthetics, such as N2O (used in anaesthesia)
Disulfiram (used to manage alcohol addiction)

Overdosage:

ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION will be administered to you only by a doctor or a nurse in a hospital and so it is unlikely to receive an overdose. However, consult your doctor or nurse if you experience any unusual symptoms after ISOTROY 30 LIQUID FOR INHALATION administration such as hypotension (low blood pressure) and respiratory depression or cessation of breathing.

name: Sosrane Liquid 100ml
introduction:
Introduction About SOSRANE LIQUID

SOSRANE LIQUID contains Isoflurane which belongs to a group of medicines known as General Anaesthetics. SOSRANE LIQUID is used for induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia during surgeries.

General Anaesthesia can be defined as a state of controlled unconsciousness. There is temporary reduction in activity of central nervous system in brain which in result causes complete loss of sensation in body and loss of consciousness, which is required during surgery.

SOSRANE LIQUID is not recommended for use in patients with or family history of rapid rise in body temperature during anaesthesia (a condition known as malignant hyperthermia). SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in patients having liver, heart, kidney or lung problems, increased intracranial pressure, myasthenia gravis (muscle weakness) or diabetes.

SOSRANE LIQUID is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless it is clearly necessary. SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it is not known whether it passes through the breast milk. SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in children so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in elderly patients aged above 65 years. The most common side effects of using SOSRANE LIQUID are agitation, breath holding, chills or shivering, cough, change in mental abilities, spasm of vocal cords, nausea and vomiting. Consult your physician in case any of the symptoms worsen.

mechanismOfAction:
How SOSRANE LIQUID Works

SOSRANE LIQUID is a general anaesthetic that works by temporarily reducing the activity of the body’s central nervous system. This leads to complete loss of sensation in the body, including loss of consciousness and allowing surgery to be carried out without any pain or distress.

SOSRANE LIQUID is administered by your doctor through a vaporizer. Your doctor will decide the exact dose and duration of management for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition and the type of operation you are having and when SOSRANE LIQUID is to be given.

name: Fresofol 1% Injection 20ml
introduction:
Introduction About FRESOFOL 1% INJECTION

FRESOFOL 1% INJECTION contains Propofol which belongs to the group of medicines called General Anaesthetic agents. It is used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness in patients so that surgical procedures can be performed. Unconsciousness caused by propofol is completely reversed once the effect of the medicine wears off. It can also be used to induce sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

FRESOFOL 1% INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anesthesiologist into the vein (intravenously). It is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 1 month or older). It is mostly used in combination with other local anaesthetics to achieve faster results.

Before receiving FRESOFOL 1% INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have fits, high blood cholesterol levels or dehydration as a precaution.

FRESOFOL 1% INJECTION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Breastfeeding should be stopped for 24 hours or until the effect of the medicine completely wears off, as this medicine may pass to the nursing infant through the breast milk.

The most common side effects of receiving FRESOFOL 1% INJECTION are pain, swelling and redness at the site of injection, low blood pressure, slow heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, headache and flushing. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

How FRESOFOL 1% INJECTION Works

FRESOFOL 1% INJECTION is a general anaesthetic agent. It produces loss of consciousness by potentiating the actions of certain brain chemicals (GABA) any by decreasing the flow of certain ions (chloride) across the nerve cells that is required to maintain alertness.

name: THEMICAINE Jelly 30gm
introduction:
Introduction About THEMICAINE JELLY

THEMICAINE JELLY contains Lignocaine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Local anaesthetic agents. It causes numbness of body parts at sites where it has been applied. It is used for temporary relief of pain and discomfort associated with skin abrasions, sun burns, insect bites, sore nipples, haemorrhoids (piles), anal fissures, bed sores, shingles, or cold sores (painful skin rash or blisters around the mouth due to viral infections).

It can also be used to relieve pain following circumcision in children (a surgery that removes the foreskin from the human penis) and to soothe itching around the rectum, anus (pruritus ani), or female genitalia (vulva).

It also relieves pain caused by oral sores and can numb the mouth and throat prior to any dental procedures (such as scaling or denture fixing).

It acts as an anaesthetic lubricant for catheterization, intubation, and other diagnostic procedures (such as proctoscopy, rectoscopy, cystoscopy, gastroscopy, bronchoscopy, esophagoscopy, etc.).

If you are managed with THEMICAINE JELLY in your oral cavity, avoid oral foods or chewing gums for at least 60 minutes or until sensation comes back in your mouth. This is because you may experience trouble swallowing or accidentally bite your tongue or cheek muscles during this period.

Before using THEMICAINE JELLY, inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney, or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any infections or injuries at the site of application as a precaution.

THEMICAINE JELLY can be used for pregnant and breastfeeding women if considered necessary. It is generally safe and well tolerated without any major side effects. However, if you experience any skin rash or irritation on the application site or feel drowsy, consult your doctor for advice.

mechanismOfAction:
How THEMICAINE JELLY Works

THEMICAINE JELLY is a local anaesthetic agent. It reduces pain sensation and causes numbness in body parts by blocking the flow of certain ions (sodium ions) through the nerves that cause pain sensation. As a result, it limits the transfer of pain signals from the peripheral part of the body (i.e., the face, hands, legs, abdomen, pelvis, genitals, or where the medicine has been applied) to the brain, which ultimately leads to loss of sensation.
usageDetails:
How to use THEMICAINE JELLY

THEMICAINE JELLY should be used under proper medical supervision. It is administered by the physician in the region where anesthesia is required. However, it can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor.

Take a small quantity of THEMICAINE JELLY and apply it to the required areas. Avoid contact with THEMICAINE JELLY with your eyes.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight, health condition, and sites where numbness is required in the body.

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before using THEMICAINE JELLY, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines, such as:

Mexiletine, amiodarone (used to manage an uneven heartbeat)
Cimetidine (a medicine used to manage stomach ulcers)
Beta-blockers such as atenolol, propranolol, and bisoprolol (used to manage high blood pressure)
Nitrates (such as nitric oxide and nitroglycerin) are used to improve blood flow
Other local anaesthetic agents (such as bupivacaine, proparacaine, ropivacaine, mepivacaine, prilocaine, procaine, and tetracaine)
Antibiotics (used to manage bacterial infections) such as PABA, nitrofurantoin, dapsone, and sulfasalazine

Anti-epileptic agents (used to manage fits) Ex. phenytoin, sodium valproate, phenobarbital
Metoclopramide (a medicine used to manage nausea and vomiting)

If you or anyone else has applied excessive THEMICAINE JELLY, wipe off the excess with a paper towel or tissue paper. If your child or anyone else accidentally swallowed THEMICAINE JELLY, contact your doctor immediately or visit a nearby hospital immediately, as it may lead to a severe decrease in low blood pressure.

name: Oculan 1% Injection 10X2ml
introduction:
Introduction About OCULAN 1% INJECTION

OCULAN 1% INJECTION contains Lignocaine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Local anaesthetic agents. It is used to cause numbness (loss of sensation) of body parts in the regions where it has been administered (local anesthesia). It is generally used prior to spinal anesthesia or before surgical procedures to cause a temporary loss of sensation. It also helps to control the heartbeat in patients with arrythmia (an irregular heartbeat).

OCULAN 1% INJECTION will be given to you only by a trained anaesthesiologist around the areas (such as hands, legs, abdomen, pelvis, and spine) locally where loss of sensation (numbness) is required.

Before receiving OCULAN 1% INJECTION, inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney, or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any breathing disorders, blood problems, epilepsy, glaucoma, stroke, dehydration, low blood potassium levels, or muscle weakness.

OCULAN 1% INJECTION should be used in pregnant or breastfeeding women only if considered necessary by the physician. The most common side effects of receiving OCULAN 1% INJECTION are nausea, slow heart rate, dizziness, lower back pain, difficulty walking, and an inability to control urine or bowel movements. Inform your doctor if any of these side effects worsen.

How OCULAN 1% INJECTION Works

OCULAN 1% INJECTION is an anaesthetic agent. OCULAN 1% INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anaesthesiologist. It can be administered locally to the region where loss of sensation (numbness) is required or can be administered in a vein, around the spinal cord, or a nerve to cause numbness during surgeries (caesarean section or other major surgeries) to stop pain sensation.

name: DEXEM 50mcg Injection 0.5ml
introduction:
Introduction About DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION contains Dexmedetomidine which belongs to the group of medicines called Sedatives. It is used in adults to provide sedation (a state of calm, drowsiness or sleep) in hospital intensive care settings. It is also used to provide conscious sedation during different diagnostic or surgical procedures.

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with heart rhythm disorders, a history of stroke or other serious conditions affecting the blood supply to the brain. Consult your doctor before receiving this medicine.

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from severe kidney or liver problems, abnormally slow heart rate, low blood pressure or chronic hypertension, low blood volume (Ex. after bleeding), diabetes mellitus, neurological disorder (Ex. head or spinal cord injury or stroke). Consult your doctor before receiving this medicine.

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION should not be used during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless clearly necessary. Consult your doctor before receiving this medicine.

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients aged above 65 years. Consult your doctor before receiving this medicine.

The most common side effects of receiving DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION are slow heart rate, low or high blood pressure, change in breathing pattern. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms get worse.
uses: To provide sedation for adult patients in hospital intensive care settings
To provide conscious sedation during different diagnostic or surgical procedures
usesDetails:
Uses Of DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION
To provide sedation for adult patients in hospital intensive care settings
To provide conscious sedation during different diagnostic or surgical procedures
mechanismOfAction:
How DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION Works

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION works by binding to certain receptors in the brain called alpha-2 adrenoceptors and manages the release of norepinephrine (a chemical called neurotransmitter). Thus providing pain relief during procedures.
usageDetails:
How to use DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION is administered to you by a doctor or nurse prior to and/or during diagnostic or surgical procedures requiring sedation (procedural/conscious sedation). It is diluted and it is given to you as an infusion (drip) into your veins.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending upon your age, body weight, general condition of health, the level of sedation needed and how you respond to the medicine.
sideEffects: Change in breathing pattern or shortness of breath
Hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not present)

Common
Slow or fast heart rate
Low or high blood pressure
Change in breathing pattern or shortness of breath
Chest pain or heart attack
Nausea, vomiting or dry mouth
Restlessness
High temperature
Uncommon
Hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not present)
Reduced heart function, cardiac arrest
Swelling of the stomach
Thirst

warnings.details: DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary. Consult your doctor before receiving DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION.
DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION should not be used in breast feeding women unless clearly necessary. Consult your doctor before receiving DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION.

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION has major impact on the ability to drive and use machines. After you have been given this medicine, you must not drive, operate machinery or work in dangerous situations until the effects are completely gone. Ask your doctor when you can start doing these activities again and when you can go back to this kind of work.
Talk to your doctor about the use of alcohol after sedation/wake-up.
DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from severe kidney problems. Consult your doctor before receiving DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION.
DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from severe liver problems. Consult your doctor before receiving DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION.
Do not receive this medicine if you are allergic to dexmedetomidine or any of the other ingredients of this medicine.

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with heart rhythm disorders (heart block grade 2 or 3), very low blood pressure which does not respond to> management. Consult your doctor before receiving this medicine.

Others

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION is not recommended for you, if you have:

Recently had a stroke or other serious condition affecting blood supply to the brain

Before receiving DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION, inform your doctor if you have:

Low blood volume (Ex. after bleeding)
Neurological disorder (Ex. head or spinal cord injury or stroke)
Ever developed a serious fever after taking some medicines called anaesthetics
Diabetes mellitus

Use in pediatrics:

The safety and efficacy of DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION in pediatric patients have not been established for procedural or ICU sedation. Consult your doctor before receiving DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION.

Use in geriatrics:

DEXEM 50MCG INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients aged above 65 years due to increased risk of low heart rate and low blood pressure. Consult your doctor before receiving this medicine.

name: Pacifol Injection 10ml
introduction:
Introduction About PACIFOL INJECTION

PACIFOL INJECTION contains Propofol which belongs to the group of medicines called General Anaesthetic agents. It is used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness in patients so that surgical procedures can be performed. Unconsciousness caused by propofol is completely reversed once the effect of the medicine wears off. It can also be used to induce sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

PACIFOL INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anesthesiologist into the vein (intravenously). It is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 1 month or older). It is mostly used in combination with other local anaesthetics to achieve faster results.

Before receiving PACIFOL INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have fits, high blood cholesterol levels or dehydration as a precaution.

PACIFOL INJECTION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Breastfeeding should be stopped for 24 hours or until the effect of the medicine completely wears off, as this medicine may pass to the nursing infant through the breast milk.

The most common side effects of receiving PACIFOL INJECTION are pain, swelling and redness at the site of injection, low blood pressure, slow heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, headache and flushing. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.
uses: Used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness prior to surgical procedures
Induces sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU)

Uses Of PACIFOL INJECTION
Used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness prior to surgical procedures
Induces sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
mechanismOfAction:
How PACIFOL INJECTION Works

PACIFOL INJECTION is a general anaesthetic agent. It produces loss of consciousness by potentiating the actions of certain brain chemicals (GABA) any by decreasing the flow of certain ions (chloride) across the nerve cells that is required to maintain alertness.

PACIFOL INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anesthesiologist into the vein (intravenously).

Your doctor/ anesthesiologist will decide the correct dose for you depending upon the age, body weight and disease condition.
sideEffects: Injection site reactions (such as pain, redness and swelling)
Withdrawal symptoms (such as abnormal behaviour, increased sweating, shakiness and anxiety)

Common
Injection site reactions (such as pain, redness and swelling)
Low blood pressure

warnings.details: PACIFOL INJECTION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Therefore, inform your doctor before receiving it.
Breastfeeding should be stopped for 24 hours or until the effect of the medicine completely wears off, as this medicine may pass to the nursing infant through the breast milk.
Do not drive or operate any heavy tools or machines until the effects of the medicine complete wears off
Avoid consumption of alcohol before receiving PACIFOL INJECTION.
PACIFOL INJECTION should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
PACIFOL INJECTION should be used with caution in patients with liver problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
Inform your doctor before receiving PACIFOL INJECTION, if you are allergic to Propofol.
PACIFOL INJECTION should be used with caution in patients with breathing disorders (such as asthma or COPD). Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
PACIFOL INJECTION should be used with caution in patients with heart disorders. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

Others

Before receiving PACIFOL INJECTION, inform your physician if you:

Ever had epilepsy (fits)
Have high blood cholesterol levels
Are dehydrated
Have mitochondrial diseases
Are generally unwell

Use in pediatrics:

PACIFOL INJECTION should be used in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) only if it is considered necessary by the physician. It is not recommended for use in neonates aged less than 1 month. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before administration.

Use in geriatrics:

PACIFOL INJECTION should be used with caution in the elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before receiving it.

It is used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness in patients so that surgical procedures can be performed. Unconsciousness caused by propofol is completely reversed once the effect of the medicine wears off. It can also be used to induce sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

CRITIFOL 1% INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anesthesiologist into the vein (intravenously). It is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 1 month or older). It is mostly used in combination with other local anaesthetics to achieve faster results.

Before receiving CRITIFOL 1% INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have fits, high blood cholesterol levels or dehydration as a precaution.

CRITIFOL 1% INJECTION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Breastfeeding should be stopped for 24 hours or until the effect of the medicine completely wears off, as this medicine may pass to the nursing infant through the breast milk.

The most common side effects of receiving CRITIFOL 1% INJECTION are pain, swelling and redness at the site of injection, low blood pressure, slow heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, headache and flushing. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

name: EPILIDO Cream 10gm
introduction:
Introduction About EPILIDO CREAM

EPILIDO CREAM is a combination of Lignocaine and Prilocaine which belongs to the group of medicines called Local Anesthetic agents. It is used to cause temporary numbness (loss of pain sensation) of the normal intact skin and genital mucosal membranes when applied topically.

It is primarily used to abolish pain signals prior to surgical and diagnostic procedures on the skin and genital areas (such as during insertion of needles or catheters, during certain painful vaccinations (such as MMR, flu, hepatitis, DPT), during minor surgeries of genital areas (such as removal of foreskin around the penis) and during laser management or other cosmetic procedures involving the skin surface).

EPILIDO CREAM can also be used to temporarily numb skin before injecting an anesthetic solution and can be used to abolish pain signals while removing dead and damaged skin/cells among patients with leg ulcers. It also provides relief from the symptoms of atopic dermatitis (red, itchy skin) in adults.

EPILIDO CREAM is suitable for use both in adults and in children (including infants and newborns). It should be used only under careful medical supervision. It will be applied to you only by a doctor or nurse at skin surfaces where loss of sensation is required.

Before EPILIDO CREAM is applied onto your skin, inform your doctor if you have any genetic disorders (like G6PD deficiency) or blood problems (such as methemoglobinemia). You must also inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before this medicine is given to you as a precaution.

EPILIDO CREAM is not suitable for use in patients with problems in ear drum. The most common side effects of using EPILIDO CREAM are paleness, redness, swelling, mild burning sensation, itching or warmth at the managed area. Consult your doctor if it bothers you.
uses: Cause temporary numbness of normal intact skin or genital mucous membrane
Provide temporary relief from the symptoms of atopic dermatitis (such as skin rash, itching)
usesDetails:
Uses Of EPILIDO CREAM

Used as topical anesthesia prior to surgical and diagnostic procedures to:

Cause temporary numbness of normal intact skin or genital mucous membrane
Provide temporary relief from the symptoms of atopic dermatitis (such as skin rash, itching)
mechanismOfAction:
How EPILIDO CREAM Works

EPILIDO CREAM is a local anesthetic medication. When applied topically, it blocks the flow of certain ions (sodium ions) through the nerves that causes pain sensation. As a result, it limits the transfer of pain signals from the peripheral part of the body (i.e., face, hands, legs, abdomen, pelvis, genitals or where the medicine has been applied) to the brain which ultimately leads to loss of sensation.
usageDetails:
How to use EPILIDO CREAM

EPILIDO CREAM should be used only under careful medical supervision. It is strictly for external use only. It will be applied to you only by a doctor or nurse at skin surfaces where loss of sensation is required.

Avoid accidental contact of this medicine with your eyes, nose, ears, mouth or anus and with damaged skin surfaces including minor cuts on the skin.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose for you depending upon your age, body weight, health condition and sites where numbness is required in the body.
sideEffects: Application site reactions (such as paleness, redness, swelling, initial mild burning sensation, itching or warmth at the managed area)
Signs of allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue causing difficulty in breathing or swallowing, fainting)
Signs of methemoglobinemia (such as lack of oxygen, breathlessness)
sideEffectsDetails:
Side Effects Of EPILIDO CREAM
Common
Application site reactions (such as paleness, redness, swelling, initial mild burning sensation, itching or warmth at the managed area)
Uncommon
Skin irritation
Rare

Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects after using EPILIDO CREAM:

Signs of allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue causing difficulty in breathing or swallowing, fainting)
Signs of methemoglobinemia (such as lack of oxygen, breathlessness)

warnings.details: EPILIDO CREAM should be used with caution among pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before application.
EPILIDO CREAM should be used with caution among breastfeeding women. Therefore, inform your doctor before application.
EPILIDO CREAM is unlikely to affect your ability for driving or handling heavy tools or machines.
Talk to your doctor before EPILIDO CREAM is applied onto your skin, if you are allergic to lignocaine, prilocaine or to any other local anesthetic agents (such as bupivacaine).

EPILIDO CREAM can be used in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) if prescribed by the physician. However, it should not be used on the genital areas of children aged below 12 years. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before application.
EPILIDO CREAM should be used with caution in the elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before application.

Others

EPILIDO CREAM is not recommended for use if you:

Have cuts or bruises on the skin surface
Have open wound (apart from leg ulcers)
Have problems in ear drum (such as impaired ear drum)

Before EPILIDO CREAM is applied onto your skin, inform your physician if you:

Have G6PD deficiency (a genetic problem)
Have methemoglobinemia (abnormal amount of blood components)

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before EPILIDO CREAM is applied onto your skin, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines such as:

Medicines used to manage irregular heartbeat (such as digoxin, amiodarone procainamide)
Live vaccines (such as BCG, MMR)
Anti-epileptic agents (used to manage fits) Ex. phenytoin, sodium valproate, phenobarbital
Nitrofurantoin (a medicine used to manage urinary tract infections)
Sulphonamides (used to manage bacterial infections) such as sulfasalazine
Cimetidine (a medicine used to manage stomach ulcers)
Beta-blockers such as atenolol, propranolol, bisoprolol (used to manage high blood pressure)
Other local anesthetic agents (such as bupivacaine, proparacaine, ropivacaine, mepivacaine, procaine, tetracaine)

Overdosage:

EPILIDO CREAM will be applied to you only by a doctor or a nurse onto the skin. Therefore, it is unlikely to receive an overdose. However, if you experience any unusual side effects such as dizziness, blurred vision, tingling sensation around the mouth, numbness of tongue, abnormal taste or ringing in the ears, contact your doctor or visit the nearby hospital immediately.

Are dehydrated
Have mitochondrial diseases
Are generally unwell

RAPIFOL 10MG INFUSION should be used with caution in the elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before receiving it.

name: Ropin 0.5 Injection 20ml
introduction:
Introduction About ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION contains Ropivacaine which belongs to the group of medicines called Local Anaesthetics. It is used in children and adults of all ages for acute pain management. It numbs (anaesthetises) parts of the body Ex. after surgery.

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients suffering from hypovolemia (decreased volume of blood). Consult your doctor before receiving it.

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from lung, liver, kidney, heart diseases, porphyria (a blood disorder). Consult your doctor before receiving it.

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used during pregnancy only if clearly necessary and inform your doctor if you are breast feeding as it is not known whether this medicine passes into breast milk.

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used with caution in new-born and children below 12 years of age and in elderly patients above 65 years of age. Consult your doctor before receiving it.

The most common side effects of receiving ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION are low blood pressure causing dizziness or light-headedness, nausea. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen.
uses: For acute pain management in children and adults of all ages
To numbs (anaesthetises) parts of the body Ex. after surgery
usesDetails:
Uses Of ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION
For acute pain management in children and adults of all ages
To numbs (anaesthetises) parts of the body Ex. after surgery
mechanismOfAction:
How ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION Works

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION works by stopping the nerves from being able to pass pain messages to the brain. Thus ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION will stop you feeling pain, heat or cold in where it is used however you may still have other feelings like pressure or touch.
usageDetails:
How to use ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor as an injection or as an infusion into the region or near to the body part that needs to be numbed or as an epidural injection (into the area around the spinal cord). Your doctor will decide the exact dose and duration of management depending upon the type of pain relief you need, age, body weight and condition.
sideEffects: Low blood pressure causing dizziness, light-headedness
Numbness of the lips, tongue and around the mouth

Serious allergic reactions (such as anaphylaxis) include sudden onset of rash, itching or hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or other parts of the body causing shortness of breath, wheezing or difficulty breathing
Signs and symptoms of methemoglobinemia include pale, grey or blue-coloured skin, headache, rapid heart rate, shortness of breath, light-headedness and fatigue

Stop receiving ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION and consult your doctor immediately in case you experience:

Serious allergic reactions (such as anaphylaxis) include sudden onset of rash, itching or hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or other parts of the body causing shortness of breath, wheezing or difficulty breathing
Signs and symptoms of methemoglobinemia include pale, grey or blue-coloured skin, headache, rapid heart rate, shortness of breath, light-headedness and fatigue

warnings.details: ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used during pregnancy only if clearly necessary. Contact your doctor before receiving it.
If you are breastfeeding, ask your doctor for advice as it is not known whether this medicine passes into breast milk.
ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION can make you feel sleepy and affect your action reaction speed. Do not drive or operate machines until the next day after receiving ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION.
ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from kidney diseases and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before receiving it.
ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from liver diseases and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before receiving it.
Do not receive ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION if you are allergic to ropivacaine or to other local anaesthetics such as lidocaine, bupivacaine or any of the other ingredients of this medicine.
ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from lung diseases. Consult your doctor before receiving it.
ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from heart diseases and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before receiving it.

Others

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION is not recommended for use if you:

Have hypovolemia (decreased volume of blood)

Before receiving ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION inform your doctor if you:

Have a rare blood disorder called porphyria or family history of porphyria
Have glucose-6phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (hereditary disorder that affects red blood cells)
Have congenital or idiopathic methemoglobinemia (condition affects red blood cells)

Use in paediatrics:

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used with caution in new-born and children below 12 years of age. Consult your doctor before receiving it.

Use in geriatrics:

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients above 65 years of age. Consult your doctor before receiving it.

ROPIN 0.5 INJECTION will be administered to you only by a doctor in a hospital and so it is unlikely to receive an overdose. However, consult your doctor or nurse if you experience any unusual symptoms such as dizziness or light headedness, numbness of lips, tongue, around the mouth, hearing problems, visual problems, problems with your speech, muscle twitching, tremors, trembling, fits and loss of consciousness.

name: PRILIDO Cream 5gm
introduction:
Introduction About PRILIDO CREAM

PRILIDO CREAM is a combination of Lignocaine and Prilocaine which belongs to the group of medicines called Local Anesthetic agents. It is used to cause temporary numbness (loss of pain sensation) of the normal intact skin and genital mucosal membranes when applied topically.

It is primarily used to abolish pain signals prior to surgical and diagnostic procedures on the skin and genital areas (such as during insertion of needles or catheters, during certain painful vaccinations (such as MMR, flu, hepatitis, DPT), during minor surgeries of genital areas (such as removal of foreskin around the penis) and during laser management or other cosmetic procedures involving the skin surface).

PRILIDO CREAM can also be used to temporarily numb skin before injecting an anesthetic solution and can be used to abolish pain signals while removing dead and damaged skin/cells among patients with leg ulcers. It also provides relief from the symptoms of atopic dermatitis (red, itchy skin) in adults.

PRILIDO CREAM is suitable for use both in adults and in children (including infants and newborns). It should be used only under careful medical supervision. It will be applied to you only by a doctor or nurse at skin surfaces where loss of sensation is required.

Before PRILIDO CREAM is applied onto your skin, inform your doctor if you have any genetic disorders (like G6PD deficiency) or blood problems (such as methemoglobinemia). You must also inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before this medicine is given to you as a precaution.

PRILIDO CREAM is not suitable for use in patients with problems in ear drum. The most common side effects of using PRILIDO CREAM are paleness, redness, swelling, mild burning sensation, itching or warmth at the managed area. Consult your doctor if it bothers you.
uses: Cause temporary numbness of normal intact skin or genital mucous membrane
Provide temporary relief from the symptoms of atopic dermatitis (such as skin rash, itching)
usesDetails:
Uses Of PRILIDO CREAM

Used as topical anesthesia prior to surgical and diagnostic procedures to:

Cause temporary numbness of normal intact skin or genital mucous membrane
Provide temporary relief from the symptoms of atopic dermatitis (such as skin rash, itching)
mechanismOfAction:
How PRILIDO CREAM Works

PRILIDO CREAM is a local anesthetic medication. When applied topically, it blocks the flow of certain ions (sodium ions) through the nerves that causes pain sensation. As a result, it limits the transfer of pain signals from the peripheral part of the body (i.e., face, hands, legs, abdomen, pelvis, genitals or where the medicine has been applied) to the brain which ultimately leads to loss of sensation.
usageDetails:
How to use PRILIDO CREAM

PRILIDO CREAM should be used only under careful medical supervision. It is strictly for external use only. It will be applied to you only by a doctor or nurse at skin surfaces where loss of sensation is required.

Avoid accidental contact of this medicine with your eyes, nose, ears, mouth or anus and with damaged skin surfaces including minor cuts on the skin.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose for you depending upon your age, body weight, health condition and sites where numbness is required in the body.
sideEffects: Application site reactions (such as paleness, redness, swelling, initial mild burning sensation, itching or warmth at the managed area)
Signs of allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue causing difficulty in breathing or swallowing, fainting)
Signs of methemoglobinemia (such as lack of oxygen, breathlessness)
sideEffectsDetails:

Common
Application site reactions (such as paleness, redness, swelling, initial mild burning sensation, itching or warmth at the managed area)
Uncommon
Skin irritation
Rare

Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects after using PRILIDO CREAM:

Signs of allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue causing difficulty in breathing or swallowing, fainting)
Signs of methemoglobinemia (such as lack of oxygen, breathlessness)

warnings.details: PRILIDO CREAM should be used with caution among pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before application.
PRILIDO CREAM should be used with caution among breastfeeding women. Therefore, inform your doctor before application.
PRILIDO CREAM is unlikely to affect your ability for driving or handling heavy tools or machines.
Talk to your doctor before PRILIDO CREAM is applied onto your skin, if you are allergic to lignocaine, prilocaine or to any other local anesthetic agents (such as bupivacaine).

PRILIDO CREAM can be used in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) if prescribed by the physician. However, it should not be used on the genital areas of children aged below 12 years. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before application.
PRILIDO CREAM should be used with caution in the elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before application.

Others

PRILIDO CREAM is not recommended for use if you:

Have cuts or bruises on the skin surface
Have open wound (apart from leg ulcers)
Have problems in ear drum (such as impaired ear drum)

Before PRILIDO CREAM is applied onto your skin, inform your physician if you:

Have G6PD deficiency (a genetic problem)
Have methemoglobinemia (abnormal amount of blood components)

introduction:
Introduction About SEVOTROY 50 LIQUID FOR INHALATION

SEVOTROY 50 LIQUID FOR INHALATION contains Sevoflurane, which belongs to the group of medicines called Anesthetics. It is used to induce and maintain a deep, pain-free sleep (general anesthesia) in adults and children during an operation.

SEVOTROY 50 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is not recommended for use in patients with liver disease, QT prolongation, or torsade de pointes, which may also be associated with QT prolongation. Consult your doctor before using it.

SEVOTROY 50 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in patients with kidney disease, respiratory depression (breathing difficulties), heart disease, low blood pressure or low blood volume or blood circulation problems, or coronary artery disease. Consult your doctor before using it.

If you are pregnant, trying to become pregnant, or are breast-feeding. Consult your doctor before receiving SEVOTROY 50 LIQUID FOR INHALATION, as the safety of this medicine in pregnancy and breastfeeding is not known.

The most common side effects of receiving SEVOTROY 50 LIQUID FOR INHALATION are restlessness, slow heart rate, low blood pressure, coughing, nausea and vomiting, and delirium. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.

name: XYNOVA GEL 30GM
introduction:
Introduction About XYNOVA

XYNOVA contains Lignocaine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Local anaesthetic agents. It causes numbness of body parts at sites where it has been applied. It is used for temporary relief of pain and discomfort associated with skin abrasions, sun burns, insect bites, sore nipples, haemorrhoids (piles), anal fissures, bed sores, shingles, or cold sores (painful skin rash or blisters around the mouth due to viral infections).

It can also be used to relieve pain following circumcision in children (a surgery that removes the foreskin from the human penis) and to soothe itching around the rectum, anus (pruritus ani), or female genitalia (vulva).

It also relieves pain caused by oral sores and can numb the mouth and throat prior to any dental procedures (such as scaling or denture fixing).

It acts as an anaesthetic lubricant for catheterization, intubation, and other diagnostic procedures (such as proctoscopy, rectoscopy, cystoscopy, gastroscopy, bronchoscopy, esophagoscopy, etc.).

If you are managed with XYNOVA in your oral cavity, avoid oral foods or chewing gums for at least 60 minutes or until sensation comes back in your mouth. This is because you may experience trouble swallowing or accidentally bite your tongue or cheek muscles during this period.

Before using XYNOVA, inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney, or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any infections or injuries at the site of application as a precaution.

XYNOVA can be used for pregnant and breastfeeding women if considered necessary. It is generally safe and well tolerated without any major side effects. However, if you experience any skin rash or irritation on the application site or feel drowsy, consult your doctor for advice.

mechanismOfAction:
How XYNOVA Works

XYNOVA is a local anaesthetic agent. It reduces pain sensation and causes numbness in body parts by blocking the flow of certain ions (sodium ions) through the nerves that cause pain sensation. As a result, it limits the transfer of pain signals from the peripheral part of the body (i.e., the face, hands, legs, abdomen, pelvis, genitals, or where the medicine has been applied) to the brain, which ultimately leads to loss of sensation.
usageDetails:
How to use XYNOVA

XYNOVA should be used under proper medical supervision. It is administered by the physician in the region where anesthesia is required. However, it can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor.

Take a small quantity of XYNOVA and apply it to the required areas. Avoid contact with XYNOVA with your eyes.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight, health condition, and sites where numbness is required in the body.

Introduction About ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION contains Isoflurane which belongs to a group of medicines known as General Anaesthetics. ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is used for induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia during surgeries.

General Anaesthesia can be defined as a state of controlled unconsciousness. There is temporary reduction in activity of central nervous system in brain which in result causes complete loss of sensation in body and loss of consciousness, which is required during surgery.

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is not recommended for use in patients with or family history of rapid rise in body temperature during anaesthesia (a condition known as malignant hyperthermia). ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in patients having liver, heart, kidney or lung problems, increased intracranial pressure, myasthenia gravis (muscle weakness) or diabetes.

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless it is clearly necessary. ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it is not known whether it passes through the breast milk. ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in children so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in elderly patients aged above 65 years. The most common side effects of using ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION are agitation, breath holding, chills or shivering, cough, change in mental abilities, spasm of vocal cords, nausea and vomiting. Consult your physician in case any of the symptoms worsen.

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it is not known whether it may pass through the breast milk. Consult your doctor for advice.
ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION affects your mental alertness for 2-4 days. Do not drive or operate machines after administration of ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION.
ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in patients with kidney disease. Consult your doctor for advice.

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is not recommended for use in patients with a history of hepatitis due to a halogenated inhalational anaesthetic or a history of unexplained moderate to severe hepatic dysfunction (Ex. jaundice associated with fever and/or eosinophilia) after anaesthesia with ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION or other halogenated inhalational anaesthetics. Consult your doctor for advice.
Do not use ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION if you are allergic to isoflurane, other halogenated agents or any of the other ingredients of medicine.

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in patients having respiratory problems such as bronchoconstriction (tightening of air sacs in lungs causing coughing, wheezing, shortness of breath). Consult your doctor for advice.

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in patients suffering from heart problems such as coronary heart disease, arrythmias (irregular heartbeat), QT prolongation, Torsade’s De pointes (a specific type of raised heart rate), low blood pressure or low blood volume. Consult your doctor for advice.

Others

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION is not recommended for use if you:

Or anyone in your family, are susceptible to rapid rise in body temperature during anaesthesia (a condition known as malignant hyperthermia)
Are contraindicated to general anaesthesia

Before receiving ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION inform your doctor if you have:

Mitochondrial disease
Increased intracranial pressure (increase in pressure in brain)
Duchenne muscular dystrophy (inherited muscular weakness)
Myasthenia gravis (muscle weakness)
A disease or illness which is not related to condition for which you are undergoing surgery (Ex. severe headache, nausea, vomiting, neuromuscular disease)
Cancer
Diabetes
Weakness
Previously been given an inhaled anaesthetic, especially in the last 3 months
Reacted badly after previous administration of ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION or other similar anaesthetics (Ex. development of jaundice, fever, liver or blood problems)

Use in Paediatrics:

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in children as it may cause increase in saliva flow and respiratory secretions and cause laryngospasm (spasm of vocal cord). Consult your child’s doctor for advice.

Use in Geriatrics:

ISOTROY 250 LIQUID FOR INHALATION should be used with caution in elderly patients aged above 65 years of age as it may require dose adjustments. Consult your doctor for advice.

name: Neorof 10mg Infusion 50ml
introduction:
Introduction About NEOROF 10MG INFUSION

NEOROF 10MG INFUSION contains Propofol which belongs to the group of medicines called General Anaesthetic agents. It is used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness in patients so that surgical procedures can be performed. Unconsciousness caused by propofol is completely reversed once the effect of the medicine wears off. It can also be used to induce sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

NEOROF 10MG INFUSION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anesthesiologist into the vein (intravenously). It is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 1 month or older). It is mostly used in combination with other local anaesthetics to achieve faster results.

Before receiving NEOROF 10MG INFUSION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have fits, high blood cholesterol levels or dehydration as a precaution.

NEOROF 10MG INFUSION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Breastfeeding should be stopped for 24 hours or until the effect of the medicine completely wears off, as this medicine may pass to the nursing infant through the breast milk.

The most common side effects of receiving NEOROF 10MG INFUSION are pain, swelling and redness at the site of injection, low blood pressure, slow heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, headache and flushing. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

Uses Of NEOROF 10MG INFUSION
Used to cause partial or complete loss of consciousness prior to surgical procedures
Induces sleep in patients receiving artificial respiration in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
mechanismOfAction:
How NEOROF 10MG INFUSION Works

NEOROF 10MG INFUSION is a general anaesthetic agent. It produces loss of consciousness by potentiating the actions of certain brain chemicals (GABA) any by decreasing the flow of certain ions (chloride) across the nerve cells that is required to maintain alertness.

NEOROF 10MG INFUSION will be given to you only by a doctor or by a trained anesthesiologist into the vein (intravenously).

Your doctor/ anesthesiologist will decide the correct dose for you depending upon the age, body weight and disease condition.

warnings.details: NEOROF 10MG INFUSION is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Therefore, inform your doctor before receiving it.
Breastfeeding should be stopped for 24 hours or until the effect of the medicine completely wears off, as this medicine may pass to the nursing infant through the breast milk.
Do not drive or operate any heavy tools or machines until the effects of the medicine complete wears off
Avoid consumption of alcohol before receiving NEOROF 10MG INFUSION.
NEOROF 10MG INFUSION should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
NEOROF 10MG INFUSION should be used with caution in patients with liver problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
Inform your doctor before receiving NEOROF 10MG INFUSION, if you are allergic to Propofol.
NEOROF 10MG INFUSION should be used with caution in patients with breathing disorders (such as asthma or COPD). Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
NEOROF 10MG INFUSION should be used with caution in patients with heart disorders. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

Others

Before receiving NEOROF 10MG INFUSION, inform your physician if you:

Ever had epilepsy (fits)
Have high blood cholesterol levels
Are dehydrated
Have mitochondrial diseases
Are generally unwell

Use in pediatrics:

NEOROF 10MG INFUSION should be used in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) only if it is considered necessary by the physician. It is not recommended for use in neonates aged less than 1 month. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before administration.

Use in geriatrics:

NEOROF 10MG INFUSION should be used with caution in the elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before receiving it.

name: Sosrane Liquid 30ml
introduction:
Introduction About SOSRANE LIQUID

SOSRANE LIQUID contains Isoflurane which belongs to a group of medicines known as General Anaesthetics. SOSRANE LIQUID is used for induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia during surgeries.

General Anaesthesia can be defined as a state of controlled unconsciousness. There is temporary reduction in activity of central nervous system in brain which in result causes complete loss of sensation in body and loss of consciousness, which is required during surgery.

SOSRANE LIQUID is not recommended for use in patients with or family history of rapid rise in body temperature during anaesthesia (a condition known as malignant hyperthermia). SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in patients having liver, heart, kidney or lung problems, increased intracranial pressure, myasthenia gravis (muscle weakness) or diabetes.

SOSRANE LIQUID is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless it is clearly necessary. SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it is not known whether it passes through the breast milk. SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in children so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in elderly patients aged above 65 years. The most common side effects of using SOSRANE LIQUID are agitation, breath holding, chills or shivering, cough, change in mental abilities, spasm of vocal cords, nausea and vomiting. Consult your physician in case any of the symptoms worsen.

Induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia during surgeries

How SOSRANE LIQUID Works

SOSRANE LIQUID is a general anaesthetic that works by temporarily reducing the activity of the body’s central nervous system. This leads to complete loss of sensation in the body, including loss of consciousness and allowing surgery to be carried out without any pain or distress.

SOSRANE LIQUID is administered by your doctor through a vaporizer. Your doctor will decide the exact dose and duration of management for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition and the type of operation you are having and when SOSRANE LIQUID is to be given.

SOSRANE LIQUID affects your mental alertness for 2-4 days. Do not drive or operate machines after administration of SOSRANE LIQUID.
SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in patients with kidney disease. Consult your doctor for advice.

SOSRANE LIQUID is not recommended for use in patients with a history of hepatitis due to a halogenated inhalational anaesthetic or a history of unexplained moderate to severe hepatic dysfunction (Ex. jaundice associated with fever and/or eosinophilia) after anaesthesia with SOSRANE LIQUID or other halogenated inhalational anaesthetics. Consult your doctor for advice.
Do not use SOSRANE LIQUID if you are allergic to isoflurane, other halogenated agents or any of the other ingredients of medicine.

SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in patients having respiratory problems such as bronchoconstriction (tightening of air sacs in lungs causing coughing, wheezing, shortness of breath). Consult your doctor for advice.

SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in patients suffering from heart problems such as coronary heart disease, arrythmias (irregular heartbeat), QT prolongation, Torsade’s De pointes (a specific type of raised heart rate), low blood pressure or low blood volume. Consult your doctor for advice.

Others

SOSRANE LIQUID is not recommended for use if you:

Or anyone in your family, are susceptible to rapid rise in body temperature during anaesthesia (a condition known as malignant hyperthermia)
Are contraindicated to general anaesthesia

Before receiving SOSRANE LIQUID inform your doctor if you have:

Mitochondrial disease
Increased intracranial pressure (increase in pressure in brain)
Duchenne muscular dystrophy (inherited muscular weakness)
Myasthenia gravis (muscle weakness)
A disease or illness which is not related to condition for which you are undergoing surgery (Ex. severe headache, nausea, vomiting, neuromuscular disease)
Cancer
Diabetes
Weakness
Previously been given an inhaled anaesthetic, especially in the last 3 months
Reacted badly after previous administration of SOSRANE LIQUID or other similar anaesthetics (Ex. development of jaundice, fever, liver or blood problems)

Use in Paediatrics:

SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in children as it may cause increase in saliva flow and respiratory secretions and cause laryngospasm (spasm of vocal cord). Consult your child’s doctor for advice.

Use in Geriatrics:

SOSRANE LIQUID should be used with caution in elderly patients aged above 65 years of age as it may require dose adjustments. Consult your doctor for advice.

Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before administration of SOSRANE LIQUID, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Medicines used for management of high blood pressure and heart diseases (Ex. labetalol, acebutolol, atenolol, nifedipine, verapamil, amlodipine)
Opioids such as codeine, fentanyl, tramadol (used for management of severe pain)
Zolpidem, zopiclone (medicines used for management of insomnia)
Epinephrine, isoprenaline, ephedrine, norepinephrine (medicines for management of hypersensitivity, heart diseases, respiratory problems, etc.)
Amphetamine, dextroamphetamine (medicines used for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder)
Ephedrine (used for decongestion)
Isoniazid (used for management of tuberculosis)
Phenelzine, selegiline, isocarboxazid, St. John’s Wort (medicines used for management of depression)
Succinylcholine, atracurium, pancuronium, rocuronium, vecuronium (muscle relaxants used in anaesthesia)
Inhalational anaesthetics, such as N2O (used in anaesthesia)
Disulfiram (used to manage alcohol addiction)

Overdosage:

SOSRANE LIQUID will be administered to you only by a doctor or a nurse in a hospital and so it is unlikely to receive an overdose. However, consult your doctor or nurse if you experience any unusual symptoms after SOSRANE LIQUID administration such as hypotension (low blood pressure) and respiratory depression or cessation of breathing.
